article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Z × Kush Mints
Breeder: Alien Labs
THC Content: 23–30%
CBD Content: Typically very low or negligible
Terpene Profile: D-limonene , beta-caryophyllene , linalool
Primary Flavors: Sweet cereal, grapefruit, apricot
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September to early October
Indoor Yield: 600–700 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 1,000–1,400 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Xeno feels like two different cannabis profiles compressed into the same flower. The first impression is bright and almost playful: sugary citrus, tropical fruit, grapefruit, and something reminiscent of sweet breakfast cereal. A moment later, Kush Mints pulls the aroma downward into diesel, herbs, earth, and cool mint. Alien Labs created that contrast by crossing Z with Kush Mints, and the company still identifies those exact parents as the official lineage. Its current description compares the flavor to Trix cereal and highlights D-limonene, beta-caryophyllene, and linalool among the prominent terpenes.

The finished marijuana carries equally distinctive visual traits. Flowers tend to remain tight and compact rather than fluffy, with pale green tissue, orange-to-yellow pistils, occasional purple shading, and enough trichome coverage to give mature buds a crystalline appearance. Despite the candy-forward aroma, the effects lean heavier than the flavor suggests. Alien Labs classifies Xeno as an indica-dominant hybrid and describes its high as something capable of leaving the consumer feeling as though they are drifting away from ordinary surroundings.
Genetics and Lineage

The breeder-confirmed genetics are Z × Kush Mints. Alien Labs uses the shortened name “Z” for the famously sweet candy-fruit cultivar commonly associated with Zkittlez genetics, while Kush Mints contributes the darker Kush, earth, mint, and fuel characteristics. The same lineage is also preserved in Alien Labs breeding projects such as Agent X, where the company specifically identifies Xeno #1 as Z × Kush Mints.

Z brings much of the bright tropical sweetness. Its influence can appear as grapefruit, apricot, citrus candy, and mixed fruit rather than one narrowly defined flavor. Kush Mints shifts the offspring toward resin, structure, potency, and a denser earthy-gas finish. Instead of allowing the fruit parent to dominate completely, the selected Xeno cut holds enough diesel and mint to prevent the flower from tasting like straightforward candy weed.

The cultivar’s value as breeding material has become increasingly clear. Grounded Genetics later obtained the Alien Labs-selected Xeno cut and used it in projects such as Nigiri, explicitly describing Xeno as the Alien Labs-selected Zkittlez × Kush Mints phenotype. That outside breeding use helps confirm both the lineage and the importance of the selected cut beyond Alien Labs’ own commercial flower program.
Effects and Experience

Xeno usually begins with a noticeable mental shift rather than immediate couch-lock. Mood can rise, sensory detail may feel sharper, and conversation or entertainment can become more absorbing. The early stage often carries enough brightness to feel socially comfortable despite the cultivar’s indica-dominant classification. That can make the first several minutes feel more balanced than its eventual body effect would suggest.

Physical relaxation develops progressively. The mental lift softens, muscles begin to feel heavier, and the experience may turn quieter and more inward as the session continues. At moderate doses, that transition can remain smooth rather than sedating. Larger servings are much more likely to emphasize the Kush Mints side, producing significant body weight and a less functional mental state.

Modern potency varies widely. A current Alien Labs retail listing has shown Xeno flower near 29.6% THC, while another recent commercial pre-roll listed 23.52%. That variation illustrates why one permanent THC percentage should not be attached to the genetics. Consumers with limited tolerance should treat stronger batches carefully, since excessive THC may produce dry mouth, dizziness, anxiety, short-term memory disruption, or heavier sedation than expected.
Medical Benefits

Some medical marijuana consumers may prefer Xeno because the experience does not necessarily begin with immediate heaviness. Smaller amounts can preserve a degree of mental engagement while gradually introducing more physical relaxation. That progression may be preferable for people who dislike strains that move directly from the first inhalation into strong sedation.

The potency range makes dosage especially important. Flower testing near 30% THC can behave very differently from cannabis in the mid-teens, even when consumed in a similar amount. Terpene balance varies as well, meaning a limonene-forward batch may feel subjectively different from material showing more linalool, myrcene, or caryophyllene.

Xeno itself has not been clinically proven to treat insomnia, pain, anxiety, depression, or another medical condition. Anyone using cannabis medicinally should place more weight on the chemistry of the specific tested product, personal tolerance, medications, consumption method, and professional healthcare guidance than on the cultivar name alone.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Alien Labs describes Xeno through the interaction between Z sweetness and Kush Mints diesel, comparing the resulting flavor with sweet cereal. The company’s current terpene profile lists D-limonene, beta-caryophyllene, and linalool as prominent aromatic compounds. Together, those compounds help explain the contrast between bright citrus, peppery gas, and softer floral sweetness.

The fruit character is more complex than generic candy. Grapefruit frequently appears first, followed by apricot, citrus zest, and tropical sweetness. Mint, damp earth, pepper, and diesel emerge after the flower is broken apart. In some batches, the combination can feel almost like fruit cereal followed by cool herbal gas.

On the inhale, the profile is usually sweeter and smoother than the raw aroma suggests. Citrus candy and ripe fruit establish the opening before mint, herbs, and earthy fuel move into the finish. Proper curing matters because the lighter grapefruit and apricot notes can disappear quickly when flower is overdried, leaving behind a simpler Kush-heavy profile.
Growing Information

Authenticated Xeno clone material has been documented at approximately eight to nine weeks of flowering. Sun Clone, which maintains an Alien Labs breeder cut, lists the plant as Zkittlez × Kush Mints with an average THC level around 26% and a balanced growth structure suitable for indoor or outdoor production.

That same cultivation source reports average indoor production around 600–700 g/m² and outdoor yields around 1,000–1,400 g per plant under favorable conditions. These should be treated as optimized cultivation benchmarks rather than guaranteed results. Root volume, vegetative time, light intensity, environment, phenotype health, and training all have substantial influence on final yield.

The plant is described as relatively resilient in warm, dry conditions and responds well to topping and low-stress training. Improving light exposure and airflow across the canopy helps dense flowering sites mature more evenly. Outdoors, an eight-to-nine-week bloom generally points toward late September or early October in many compatible Northern Hemisphere climates. As with any dense, resinous cultivar, humidity control becomes increasingly important during the final weeks.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Xeno?
Xeno is Z × Kush Mints, bred and selected by Alien Labs. The company publishes that lineage directly across its Xeno flower, pre-roll, and concentrate products.
Is Xeno indica or sativa?
Alien Labs identifies Xeno as an indica-dominant hybrid. Its effects can initially feel mentally bright and euphoric before becoming increasingly relaxing and body-centered.
How strong is the Xeno strain?
Modern commercial flower commonly lands somewhere in the 20% THC range, with some batches approaching or exceeding 30%. Recent product examples have ranged from roughly 23.5% to nearly 30% THC.
What does Xeno taste like?
Sweet citrus, grapefruit, apricot, cereal-like candy, mint, earth, and diesel define the profile. Alien Labs specifically emphasizes the sweetness of Z mixed with Kush Mints fuel.
How long does Xeno take to flower?
Authenticated Alien Labs clone material generally flowers in approximately eight to nine weeks.
Final Thoughts on Xeno

Xeno succeeds because neither side of its lineage disappears into the other. Z contributes the bright fruit, grapefruit, candy, and cereal-like sweetness, while Kush Mints supplies the structure, earth, mint, gas, and heavier physical finish. Alien Labs preserves that balance in its own description of the cultivar, identifying both the genetic formula and the limonene-caryophyllene-linalool terpene combination that helps shape its recognizable aroma.

The plant also has enough horticultural substance to support the exotic presentation. An approximately eight-to-nine-week flowering cycle, strong documented yield potential, dense flower formation, and modern THC levels reaching the upper 20s make it more than a visually impressive boutique strain. For cannabis enthusiasts drawn to candy-gas hybrids, Xeno offers a particularly clean example of the style: fruit-forward without losing its Kush depth, potent without relying entirely on raw THC numbers, and distinctive enough that Alien Labs has continued using the selected cut in later breeding work.
